alternative_explanations.explanation: Class B briefs may have arrived with shorter runway this month.

confidence.rationale: Moderate upstream evidence; the sample is small for the current window.

counter_evidence.statement: Class A projects are mostly delivered on time.

interpretation.statement: The deterioration appears specific to non-Class-A work rather than general.

limitations: Video Type is the only complexity control.

management_significance.statement: Worth a conversation about Class B scheduling before drawing conclusions.

observation.statement: 11 of 16 deadline-classifiable projects in the current window were late, against 5 of 10 before.

questions_for_management.reason: Runway and assignment context are not in Monday.
questions_for_management.text: Did Class B assignments change in September?

reasoning_summary: The late rate rose by 19 points while the other Editors improved, and the gap remains after matching the Video Type and runway mix; on-time work concentrates in Class A, so the issue is not uniform.

suggested_investigations.text: Compare runway of the late Class B projects with earlier months.

title: Ahmed's late deliveries rose in the current window
